solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notice troubled situation

definitions.meaning: to notice something is to catch sight of it, to see it
being in a fix or a tight corner, as in 'a bit of a ...'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take note of a situation that has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: to catch sight of, and a predicament or awkward position one is in.

clue.text: Greek character has a large medicine bottle

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A Greek person is carrying a big bottle of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass vial used for holding liquid medicine is this word, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Operetta delights one, or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters of these three words are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A light opera pleases someone, or perhaps it doesn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' signals rearranging the thirteen letters of DELIGHTS ONE OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, set among Venetian boatmen, is an example of an operetta.

clue.text: After brawl, dismiss one that may be on your back

definitions.text: one that may be on your back

indicators.note: After places the word for dismiss following the word for brawl

parts.note: a ruck is a rough scrimmage or fight
to sack someone is to fire them from a job

explanation.surface: Following a fight, someone is fired from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpack carried by hikers is worn strapped on the back, so this cryptic description fits.

clue.text: Prepared to study history at last

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word history

explanation.surface: A student is all set to study history at long last.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'read' a subject is the British way of saying to study it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set and equipped to act is a plain synonym for having been prepared.

clue.text: Liberal in concern, showing quality of character

indicators.note: in places the short form for Liberal inside the word for concern

parts.note: care is worry or concern
Lib is the short form for Liberal, the British political party

explanation.surface: A worried Liberal politician displays strength of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal in' tempts a solver to scramble LIBERAL, but those seven letters do not fit; 'in' is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's worth or standard of ability, as in 'a person of high ...', is their quality.

clue.text: On one's feet with regularity giving instruction to bank

parts.note: standing means upright, on one's feet
order is regular arrangement, tidiness

explanation.surface: Standing up and following a routine, someone gives directions to a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a regular fixed payment a customer tells their bank to make.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer's standing direction for a bank to pay a fixed sum regularly is exactly this banking term.

clue.text: Smart travel round a city

indicators.note: round means the words for smart and travel go around the a

parts.note: chic means stylish, smart
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A stylish tour round a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals that the two words for smart and travel wrap around the letter A between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The large US city in Illinois on Lake Michigan is an example of a city.

clue.text: Fear will collapse, getting security software

indicators.note: a thing that collapses falls apart, so the letters of fear and will are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone's fear will crumble once protective software is installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' signals the anagram of FEAR WILL, the second word doing double duty as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A program that filters network traffic to keep out intruders is a type of computer security software.

clue.text: Number returning to a centre of revolution

indicators.note: to here means joined on to, so the reversed number is attached after the a
returning means the word for the number is read backwards

parts.note: six is a number

explanation.surface: A number goes back to a central point of rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The line about which a body rotates is the pivot of its turning.

clue.text: Look into corpse covered in gore

indicators.note: into puts the word for look inside the word for corpse

parts.note: a body is a corpse
lo is an old exclamation meaning look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: A detective inspects a blood-soaked corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Smeared or stained with blood is what being covered in gore means.

clue.text: This shot an important person

parts.note: put this word before 'shot' and you get a phrase for a VIP

explanation.walkthrough: 'This' stands for the answer: followed by 'shot' it makes the phrase for a person of importance.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer plus 'shot' forms the idiom for a high-ranking, influential figure.

clue.text: Wrongly blamed for uproar

indicators.note: wrongly means incorrectly, so the letters of blamed are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone unjustly accused causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a London asylum, the word means a scene of chaos and noise.

clue.text: Decent PM's opening words?

parts.note: good means decent, satisfactory
p.m. marks the hours after noon

explanation.surface: A respectable Prime Minister begins a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister but is post meridiem, the time after noon.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting said in the hours after midday is the opening words of a conversation.

clue.text: Big bird cost Richard — quite a lot

indicators.note: quite a lot of the letters of cost Richard, but not all, make up the answer

explanation.surface: A large bird cost a man called Richard a good deal of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite a lot' looks like a price but says most of 'cost Richard' is used, dropping only C and ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless African bird is the largest living bird species, so certainly big.

clue.text: Anxious as part of guitar not quite complete

parts.note: a fret is one of the ridges across a guitar's neck

indicators.note: not quite means the word for complete loses its final letter

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: A guitarist is worried because the instrument isn't fully assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being distressed and inclined to worry is a direct synonym for anxious.

clue.text: No sound from horse heard

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a horse's cry is a neigh

explanation.surface: Someone denies hearing any noise from a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a refusal or negative vote, the opposite of yea.

clue.text: Head lost in fight with English PM

indicators.note: Head lost means the word for fight drops its first letter

parts.note: a battle is a fight

explanation.surface: A beheading in a struggle involving an English Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: He led Britain's postwar Labour government, so he is an example of a Prime Minister.

clue.text: Snobbish name received by glove puppet

indicators.note: received by means the abbreviation for name is taken inside the puppet's name

parts.note: Sooty is a yellow bear glove puppet from long-running British children's television

explanation.surface: A haughty name is given to a hand puppet.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooty is a famous British TV glove puppet, a little yellow bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking down on others as socially inferior is what being stuck-up and snobbish means.

clue.text: More certain resistance stops one taking legal action

indicators.note: stops means the letter for resistance plugs the middle of the word for a litigant

parts.note: a suer is someone who sues
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A defendant's opposition halts a litigant's case, making the outcome more sure.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative form of sure means having greater confidence or certainty.

clue.text: Asian team finally breaks through the last batsmen

indicators.note: breaks through means the chosen letter forces its way inside the cricket word

parts.note: in cricket the tail is the weak low-order batsmen who bat last

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word team

explanation.surface: A cricket side finally gets past the tail-enders.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the 'tail' is the last few batsmen in the order, usually the weakest.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a people of southern India and Sri Lanka is an example of an Asian.

clue.text: Very long sentence in biography

definitions.meaning: a prison term lasting the rest of the prisoner's days
a written account of someone's time on earth, as in 'a ... of Dickens'

explanation.surface: A lengthy prison term features in someone's biography.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a jail term served till death, and a published account of a person.

clue.text: Got rid of a sitting member, a horror of mine

parts.note: fired means dismissed, got rid of
an MP is a sitting Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP was sacked, a nightmare from someone's point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive but is a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Explosive methane gas in coal pits is a deadly danger, a terror for miners.

clue.text: Artist you would get a peep out of?

definitions.meaning: James McNeill ... was an American painter famous for his portrait of his mother

definitions.text: you would get a peep out of?
definitions.meaning: someone who makes a shrill sound through pursed lips

explanation.definitionFit: The painter James Whistler, and literally a person producing peeping notes by blowing.

clue.text: Speaking, go over and over part

indicators.note: Speaking means the word is taken by its sound when said out loud

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: An actor rehearses a part repeatedly out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's character in a play or film is their part.
